actions.body: Analysis of cognitive architectures indicates that rigid adherence to programmed objectives often ignores the critical distinction between execution and planning phases. Evidence [source-c6430c5161404598] and [source-e8ebac5ba0244992] suggests that as systems scale, the decoupling of goal-oriented planning from real-time execution monitoring creates blind spots. This structural divergence—where the system blindly follows a solution plan despite feedback suggesting environmental change—points to a necessity for metareasoning layers that can intervene when utility-function drift occurs. We must move beyond simple obedience and toward adaptive goal-directed behavior that incorporates environmental feedback as a primary constraint on execution.
actions.lede: Strict adherence to programmed objectives can inadvertently induce system failure when structural assumptions mismatch environmental realities.
actions.reason: Completing synthesis of obedience limits to provide a foundation for further experimental design, adhering to the selected topic.
actions.title: The Mechanics of Systemic Obedience Failure
